GNET - 4 elements - basic analysis

GNET - 4 elements

This is the analysis of a simplified version of the Graded Novelty Encoding Task (GNET). The original GNET used stimuli composed of five elements and six colors. To improve performance, the task was simplified by reducing stimuli to four elements (GNET4E) and three colors.

As in the original task, stimuli were algorithmically generated, allowing precise comparison between stimuli. The difference between the stimulus presented and other stimuli (several comparisons are used) is a proxy for novelty.

During familiarization, participants learned a set of 5 stimuli During the study phase, they differentiated between these and novel stimuli. During the test phase, the performed a recognition memory test for the novels intermixed with distractors. - Novels and distractors were balanced.

In the original GNET, recognition performance tended to increase monotonically with difference to familiars In the GNET4E participants showed their highest categorization performance for stimuli at intermediate levels of difference.

Difference indices

Participant level calculated variables

Exclusions

In total, the task was run 61 times.

0 runs were not completed or were duplicates.

We excluded 3 participants due to low performance in the study phase. We calculated confidence intervals for the proportion of endorsed items that were previously studied (“old”) and excluded participants whose lower confidence bound fell below 0.33.

We excluded 2 participants due to missed responses in the test phase (> 20 missing responses).

This left 50 participants in the analysis.

Demography

The sample had a mean (± SD) age of 22.02 ± 4.821254.

The sample contained 45 women.

ALT - Mixed models

Use sum-to-zero contrasts so that coefficients are interpreted as deviations from the grand mean rather than comparisons with the reference level (D1). This is useful when no stimulus type serves as a theoretically meaningful baseline condition.
